main_text.p: Quod fit tam in infimo aere supra terram, quàm in ipsis cavernosis locis subtus terram.
Simile quid nebulæ quandoq; apparet, quando tempore magni æstus, ob copiam siccarum exhalationum magnâ copiâ elevatarum, aer caliginosus interdiu redditur.
Adjuncta horum meteororum, sunt pictura & colorationes informes aliæ: factæ vel à lumine certarum stellarum, vel ab inflammata exhalatione aliqua.
A stellarum lumine pictura in nube & nebula communiter fit, Halo dicta. in nube autem sola fiunt, tum parelii & paraselenæ, tum iris.
Halo est pictura circuli colorati, circa stellam clariorem in nube vel nebula, quæ inter visum nostrum & stellam æquabilis minusq;, crassa interjicitur, efformata.

Hæc ut fiat, primum necesse est, ut per nebulam aut nubem, exiguæ æquabilisq; densitatis, (qualis rarò compingitur: unde etiam sæpius in nebula, quàm nube, Halo conspicitur) circumcirca eodem modo, & ad æquales angulos, radii luminosi ad nostrum visum refringi queant.

Quare sub Luna creberrimè apparent halones, quòd ejus debile lumen facilè in corpore vaporoso, minùs etiam crasso, frangatur. Rarissimè sub Sole: quia forte illius lumen ejusmodi nubeculam aut nebulam facilè penetrat, aut etiam discutit. Sub reliquis stellis clarioribus tantùm conspicitur, ut sub Jove, Venere, ac quibusdam insignio-

page.notes: The last word of the page is printed as "gnio-" at the foot right, continued from "insig-" on the line above; it is printed as "gnio-" and carries a hyphen, so it is a catchword-like split word; I have kept it at the end of the text as printed. Marginal references in the left margin were not legible enough to transcribe with confidence. The half-word "Hælo"/"Halo" and the line "A stellarum lumine... dicta" contain a visible overprint; the reading "dicta" is uncertain and should be checked. Some words in the passage ("stellarum", "nubeculam") may be misread due to scan quality.
